issues.legal_issue: An arbitral award should not be treated as lacking reasons or remitted on that ground when it addresses the issues raised by the parties and gives cogent reasons, despite an objection that it failed to comply with a contractual duty to give reasons.
material_facts: The parties’ construction contracts required the arbitrator to give reasons for awards in the circumstances specified by the agreement.
The arbitrator issued four awards after considering the specific issues raised by the parties and giving cogent reasons for the findings.
One party objected that the arbitrator had not addressed whether the other party abandoned the work and had not given the required reasons.
The trial court upheld the awards, but the High Court remitted them to the arbitrator for reasons.
There was no allegation or finding that the arbitrator was biased or unfair, had failed to hear both parties, had failed fairly to consider their submissions, or had improperly procured the awards.
issues.conclusion: The awards were not shown to lack reasons or to be invalid for misconduct; the remand was set aside, and the awards were upheld and made rules of the court.
issues.legal_principle: The agreement required reasons in the specified circumstances. Section 16(1) of the Arbitration Act, 1940 permits remittal in the three circumstances set out in clauses (a), (b), and (c), including where an objection to the legality of the award is apparent on its face. On the facts, the awards addressed the issues and gave cogent reasons, and there was no basis to find misconduct in making them. The Court expressly did not decide the scope of sections 16 or 30. Although cases were cited by counsel, the judgment does not rely on any earlier case.

rule.if: arbitration_appeal_from_remand_for_missing_reasons and contractual_duty_to_give_reasons and awards_address_issues_with_cogent_reasons and no_other_misconduct_shown

predicates.arbitration_appeal_from_remand_for_missi: The matter is an appeal from an order remitting arbitral awards because reasons were said to be missing.
predicates.contractual_duty_to_give_reasons: The parties’ agreement required the arbitrator to give reasons in the circumstances applicable to the awards.
predicates.awards_address_issues_with_cogent_reason: The arbitrator considered the specific issues raised by the parties and gave cogent reasons for the findings in the awards.
predicates.no_other_misconduct_shown: No allegation or finding showed that the arbitrator was biased or unfair, failed to hear both parties or fairly consider their submissions, or improperly procured the awards.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a remand of arbitral awards for missing reasons, the agreement requires reasons, the awards address the parties’ issues with cogent reasons, and no other misconduct is shown, the awards are upheld and the remand is set aside.
